title: Environment snapshot + deterministic replay harness for private/VPC on‑prem benchmarking
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Build a reproducible environment snapshot + deterministic replay harness tailored for Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments to measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and detect regressions across customer environments. This ticket delivers a lightweight agent and a portable snapshot format that can capture runtime topology, model variants, request mix, KV-cache priming state, and timing characteristics so we can replay realistic, repeatable workloads in CI and in isolated repro environments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A snapshot tool that captures network topology (local NIC config, pod/node mapping), model variant metadata (weights hash, quantization profile), serving runtime flags, and a compact representation of a request stream with timing (monotonic timestamps + jitter profile).
2) A deterministic replay binary that consumes a snapshot and reproduces request timing (including configurable jitter scaling) and KV cache priming, producing per-host tokens/sec and p95 latency metrics identical (within tolerance) to the recorded run for stable environments.
3) Regression detection: integration with our metrics comparer that emits a regression alert when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >15% for the same snapshot on the same hardware profile.
4) End-to-end tests + a sample customer snapshot (anonymized) stored at s3://redwood-benchmarks/private/sample-snapshots/2026-02-15.json and a dashboard link with plotted baselines.
5) Security review completed and sanitized snapshot format approved for customer sharing.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: use a protobuf-lite snapshot envelope (JSON can be an export format) to avoid large nested structures in the core. Snapshot pieces: meta.json (service versions, runtime flags), topology.json (node roles, CPU/GPU types, affinities), model-manifest.json (model name, weights sha256, quant), stream.log (ndjson lines: {ts_iso, client_id, route, num_tokens, prompt_hash, timing_offset_ms}).
Replay features: configurable clock speed (0.5x..4x), burst folding to emulate client-side backpressure, optional deterministic delay injection (seeded RNG) to simulate network jitter, KV cache priming step that replays first N unique prefixes per model to load caches.
Metrics: instrument with the existing metrics bridge so outputs include tokens/sec (per-host, aggregated), p50/p95/p99 latencies, model-variant breakdown, and dropped/request-fail counts. Output a compare.json with delta percentages for regression tooling.
Artifacts: initial repo at https://github.com/redwood/inference-bench/tree/ENG-20511, draft PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12345, confluence spec https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Env+Snapshot+and+Replay+Spec
notes: We must be careful to not capture customer PII in snapshots. The snapshot format must include a sanitization pass that hashes or removes prompt text and client identifiers. Coordinate with Legal and Security to create the sanitize whitelist. For on‑prem installs, the agent will require a temporary diagnostic token and explicit consent flow before upload. See privacy checklist in Confluence spec.
updates: 2026-02-17: spike completed — validated capturing of model metadata and runtime flags on a local VPC replica. Identified that GPU UUIDs differ across OS; switched to vendor/model+device-index fingerprint to improve portability.

2026-02-22: prototype replay produced tokens/sec within 3% of recorded run for a simple homogeneous workload. p95 matched within noise for runs without pre-warmed KV cache. Need to add KV priming to reduce cold-start variance.

2026-02-25: design review with Reliability and Privacy. Reliability requested an explicit 'no network' dry-run mode for isolated labs. Privacy requested field-level sanitization and a one-way hash for prompt fingerprints.

2026-02-28: implemented KV priming step and added jitter-seed option. Ran against anonymized customer snapshot from Partner X — detected a 12% tokens/sec regression caused by a kernel scheduling change; created follow-up ENG-20542 to triage scheduling path.
2026-03-01: security review kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-03. Preparing sanitized sample snapshot and regression baseline dashboard (internal link pending).
